title: [Pallas:TPU:SparseCore] JAX-produced lookup buffer causes vld_address_out_of_range in consumer
body:
### Description

On a TPU v6e, I can run a Pallas SparseCore consumer successfully when its
lookup-table input is a resident/static device buffer. However, the same
consumer fails when an ordinary JAX computation builds an equivalent buffer
online and passes it to the SparseCore kernel.

The producer uses regular JAX scatter/update operations. The resulting array
has the same logical shape, dtype, contents, padding, and requested device
layout as the working resident input. The producer output also matches a CPU
reference exactly before it is passed to the consumer.

The SparseCore kernel uses:

```python
pltpu.CompilerParams(needs_layout_passes=False)
```

The failure is a device-side halt such as:

```text
vld_address_out_of_range
```

Some variants also report:

```text
result_fifo_not_empty_at_task_commit
```

### Expected behavior

An array produced by an ordinary JAX computation should be consumable by a
Pallas SparseCore kernel when its shape, dtype, padding, and declared layout
match those of a resident input accepted by the same kernel.

If this producer-to-SparseCore handoff is unsupported, compilation should
reject it with a clear diagnostic instead of allowing a device-side
out-of-range load.

### Observed behavior matrix

| Producer | Consumer | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Resident/static device buffer | Pallas SparseCore | Works |
| Ordinary JAX scatter/update | Ordinary JAX lookup and aggregation | Works; exact result |
| Ordinary JAX scatter/update | Pallas SparseCore | Device halt |
| Ordinary JAX scatter/update | A separate SparseCore workload with a similar 2-D buffer | Works |

This suggests that SparseCore execution itself and ordinary JAX construction
are both functional, but one particular producer/consumer handoff or layout
combination is not.

### Variants already tested

The failure remains after trying:

1. Blocking on the JAX producer before launching the SparseCore consumer.
2. Wrapping the producer and consumer in one outer `jax.jit`.
3. Copying into a fresh device buffer with the same requested JAX layout.
4. Writing into a donated, preallocated workspace and verifying buffer reuse.
5. A 2-D SparseCore-friendly layout with a 128-element minor dimension.
6. Explicit physical padding to multiples of `8 x 128`.
7. Passing each small lookup table independently.
8. Packing all lookup tables into one contiguous buffer.
9. Building the packed representation directly in the donated workspace.
10. Fused and staged consumer variants.

All online producer outputs were checked against a CPU reference before the
SparseCore launch.

### Environment

- Device: TPU v6e
- JAX: 0.10.2
- `jaxlib`: 0.10.2
- `libtpu`: 0.0.42.1
- Python: 3.11.0rc1

### Reproduction

The current reproducer is part of a larger analytical-query experiment. I am
reducing it to standalone synthetic arrays containing one ordinary JAX scatter
producer, one resident-buffer control, and one minimal SparseCore load/probe
consumer. I can post that reproduction in a follow-up comment.
